notes: 1913 three-flat, cream painted wood over a buff brick garage and raised-floor base. Two round (bowed) bays side by side across the whole front on both upper storeys, white-framed sash, heavy ornate cornice. Ground: north half an open arched porch with a stair to the recessed entry, south half one white panel garage door and a narrow grilled service door. The buff brick base read cream like the wall and the bays swallowed the cornice; base tint strengthened toward buff, bays narrowed and made shallower so the cornice projects past their caps. Each swell bay is a deeper two-segment round bay so every storey carries a centre sash plus two curved side sashes (white frames); buff brick street storey (brick-buff kit); ground at the real left is the recessed stair entry with a dark wood door, then one white panelled garage door (panel grid on a white leaf, not a roll-up) and a narrow white service door. The round-arched porch head, the arched first-floor window, egg-and-dart bands and a swag frieze have no style key; the still is mirrored by the world east-west mirror. Smoother curved turret bays (four facets a quarter) set a little shallower so the heavier crowning cornice reads past them; pale grey-white upper wall with cream trim; the tall data street storey is tan/yellow brick carrying the raised-floor window over the garage (a framed flat glass panel under a brick lintel band, since arched heads have no key), a recessed porch opening at the real left reached by a pale stone stoop (flat step bands), one white panelled garage door with horizontal panel lines and a narrow service door; small darker brick accent squares stand in for the diamond panels. The bays still cover the two upper data storeys. Four-facet quarters left no room for side sashes, so the bays go back to two-segment curves (three sashes a storey) at a deeper projection.
